thread.title: Apple Hits $1.1 Trillion Market Cap As 5 More Nasdaq Stocks Lead

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Apple Hits $1.1 Trillion Market Cap As 5 More Nasdaq Stocks Lead
text:
Stocks today showed sluggish moves ahead of the three-day holiday weekend, but at around 2:30 p.m. ET the Nasdaq composite still held a small advance of less than 0.1% to pad its big weekly gains. Apple rose as much as 1.7% intraday, and hit a new all-time high of 228.87 in heavy turnover.
X Meanwhile, Leaderboard name Lululemon bolted 16% higher after smashing Wall Street quarterly estimates. Shares in the athleisure apparel leader have now risen 96% since it rebounded off the 10-week moving average in early February, setting up a follow-on buy point .
At 8092, the tech-centered Nasdaq is up almost 1.9% for the week, ponying up its best performance since a 2.4% gallop higher in the week ended July 6. The Nasdaq 100 edged slightly lower but still held on to a 2% weekly gain.
Amid a struggle between U.S. and Canadian trade negotiators to reach a new deal, the Dow Jones industrial average fell 0.3% and the S&P 500 slumped 0.2%. Volume is running sharply lower on both main exchanges.
On the 30-stock Dow, Boeing ( BA ) paced the downside. The aerospace titan dropped 4.56, or 1.3%, to 342.33.
Two more components in the Dow Jones industrials lost 1 point or more. They included Chevron ( CVX ) and United Technologies ( UTX ).
Boeing, a direct competitor in the midsize commercial jet market with Canada's Bombardier, is forming a new base. Shares have been trading in a range of roughly 325 to 375 for the past 2-1/2 months.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's benchmark fell 0.4% to 16,302. It's up just 0.6% since Jan. 1. The S&P 500, at 2895, holds a more than 8% year-to-date gain.
Small caps rallied modestly. The S&P SmallCap 600 rose 0.2%.
Lululemon Stock Leads Market Upside Lululemon ( LULU ) of Vancouver, Canada, surged following excellent fiscal second-quarter results in which earnings jumped 82% to 71 cents a share. That crushed the Thomson Reuters consensus view by 45%.
Revenue rose 25% to $723.5 million as the yogawear and sports apparel firm saw unusually strong e-commerce and Asia sales. The menswear category is also firing on all cylinders.
According to IBD Stock Checkup , Lululemon holds a top-drawer A rating for SMR (Sales + Profit Margins + Return on equity) on a scale of A to E. With 126 million shares outstanding, Lululemon is now squarely in large-cap territory with a market value of $19.9 billion.
IBD's Retail-Apparel/Shoes/Accessories industry group ranks a strong No. 13 among 197 IBD industry groups for six-month relative performance through Thursday's market close. Lululemon's market cap is now much bigger than apparel retailers Gap ( GPS ) ($11.6 billion) and L Brands ( LB ) ($7.3 billion).
Lululemon joined IBD Leaderboard on Feb. 7. That day, shares finished at 80.99 and were trying to rebound off the key 10-week moving average. Since then, its stock has vaulted more than 95%.
Other consumer-spending companies sharing space on Leaderboard with Lululemon include arts and crafts online commerce firm Etsy ( ETSY ) and video streaming hardware and smart TV channel provider Roku ( ROKU ). Both trade on the Nasdaq.
Etsy is expected to drive earnings 69% higher this year to 44 cents a share, which would be a record. Analysts surveyed by Thomson Reuters see Roku losing 14 cents a share this year, down from a net loss of 67 cents in 2017. Roku earned a penny a share in Q2 as revenue rose 57% to $156.8 million.
More Nasdaq Growth Stocks Show Market Leadership As seen in the " Stocks On The Move " table, fellow Nasdaq exchange members Conn's ( CONN ) and CyberArk Software ( CYBR ) posted solid gains in above-average turnover. The former is clearing a flat base with a 38.66 buy point.
That flat base sits on top of a longer base. Thus, the entire construction can be also called a base on base , which is bullish.
Also, notice on a daily chart how the stock's relative strength line is edging into new high ground. This means Conn's is outperforming the S&P 500.
Conn's, the Texas-based consumer electronics and furniture retail chain, ended six quarters of shrinking sales with a 1% rise in the July-ended fiscal second quarter. Conn's also earned 40 cents a share vs. a net loss of 5 cents a share a year ago. The Street sees fiscal Q3 profit jumping 58% to 41 cents a share.
Apple Stock Renaissance Continues Apple ( AAPL ) rose for an eighth straight session amid an ongoing resurgence in its corporate fundamentals. The Street expects this to continue as analysts on consensus see earnings lifting 28% to $11.75 in the current fiscal year ending in September, and FY 2019 profit up 15% to $13.56 a share. (Please see this earlier Stock Market Today piece on reasons why a $1.25 trillion market value for Apple is not unreasonable.)
The Cupertino, Calif., megacap tech reportedly plans to announce new iPhone models on Sept. 12.
The iPhone, Apple Watch, MacBook and digital services firm departed Leaderboard following a solid gain of nearly 22% after a May 4 breakout past a double-bottom base.
The proper buy point back then was 179.04, 10 cents above the base's middle peak of 178.94.
Integrated Device Technology ( IDTI ) helped fortify a recent rally among semiconductor firms. The expert in logic and memory chips gapped up 10% to 42.25 on news that a Japanese firm, Renesas Electronics, is considering acquiring the San Jose, Calif., company .
Other Financial Markets The yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury bond fell 2 basis points to 2.84%. On Aug. 1, the long bond yielded 3%. The current spread between the 3-month Treasury bill and the 10-year note is 75 basis points, down from 97 basis points at the start of the month.
WTI crude oil futures dipped 0.4% to $69.94 a barrel after rising to as high as $70.25 on Thursday. Crude is now up 15.7% since Jan. 1, beating both the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones industrials.
In economic news, the Chicago Purchasing Managers index showed a dip in its Business Barometer Index to 63.6 in August from 65.5 in July. It missed the Econoday consensus estimate of 63.8.
